title: Affine pinching by a surjective ring map
statement:
Let $A,D,T$ be commutative rings with identity (zero rings allowed), let $\alpha:A\twoheadrightarrow D$ be a surjective ring homomorphism, and let $\beta:T\to D$ be any ring homomorphism. Define the commutative ring
$$P=A\times_D T=\{(a,t)\in A\times T:\alpha(a)=\beta(t)\},$$
with componentwise operations. Put $E=\operatorname{Spec}D$, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $W=\operatorname{Spec}T$ and $Q=\operatorname{Spec}P$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The canonical morphisms $E\to Y$, $E\to W$, $Y\to Q$ and $W\to Q$ form a pushout square in the category of schemes [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Explicitly, for every scheme $Z$ and maps $Y\to Z$ and $W\to Z$ agreeing on $E$, there is a unique compatible map $Q\to Z$. No finiteness, Noetherianity or nonzero-ring assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0ET0, lemma-basic-example-pushout, statement. This affine lemma is stronger than the finite-map special case used here; it is not the additional global gluing statement of Tag 0E25.

proof.text: Write $\pi_A:P\to A$ and $\pi_T:P\to T$ for the projections. Give $A,T,D$ their $P$-module structures through these maps and their common composite. The sequence $0\to P\xrightarrow{(\pi_A,\pi_T)}A\oplus T\xrightarrow{\delta}D$ is exact, where $\delta(a,t)=\alpha(a)-\beta(t)$: the first arrow is injective, and its image is exactly the pairs on which $\delta$ vanishes, by the displayed definition of $P$. The equality $\alpha\pi_A=\beta\pi_T$ also proves commutativity of the asserted scheme square by contravariant functoriality of spectra.

source.place: Tag 01Z8, lemma-diagram-localize, first displayed exact sequence; elementary kernel computation

proof.text:
Fix $p=(a,t)\in P$ and put $d=\alpha(a)=\beta(t)$. Localize the sequence of step 1 at $1,p,p^2,\ldots$. Exactness of module localization gives an injection $P_p\to(A\oplus T)_p$ with image the kernel of $(A\oplus T)_p\to D_p$. Here $A_p=A_a$, $T_p=T_t$, $D_p=D_d$. Also $(A\oplus T)_p=A_a\oplus T_t$: pairs of fractions admit a common denominator by multiplying each numerator by the missing power, and the same common-denominator calculation detects equality. Consequently the canonical ring map
$$P_p\longrightarrow A_a\times_{D_d}T_t$$
is bijective. It is a ring map because both components are the localized projections and all operations in the fibre product are componentwise. In particular, $P_p\to A_a\times T_t$ is injective. No nonzero denominator assumption was used.

source.place: Tag 01Z8, lemma-diagram-localize, proof by exactness of localization (Tag 00CS)

proof.text: Let $f:Y\to Z$ and $g:W\to Z$ agree on $E$, with $Z$ any scheme. Apply [lem-sfb-fibre-product-spectrum-topology] to their underlying continuous maps. It gives a unique continuous map $h:|Q|\to|Z|$ restricting to $|f|$ and $|g|$, and the two maps into $Q$ are jointly surjective. For each $q\in Q$ choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Z$ containing $h(q)$. The principal-open basis of $Q$ gives $p\in P$ with $q\in D(p)\subseteq h^{-1}(V)$. All such pairs $(p,V)$ form an open cover of $Q$. The affine-open basis theorem supplies $V$, and does not assume intersections of affine opens are affine.

source.place: Tag 0ET0, lemma-basic-example-pushout, underlying topological pushout; affine-open realization of its sheaf argument

proof.text: For a pair $(p,V)$ of step 3, write $p=(a,t)$ and $d=\alpha(a)=\beta(t)$. The inverse images of $D(p)$ in $Y,W,E$ are respectively $D(a),D(t),D(d)$, since a prime contains the image of $p$ precisely when its contraction contains $p$. The principal-localization open immersions identify these open subschemes with $\operatorname{Spec}A_a$, $\operatorname{Spec}T_t$, $\operatorname{Spec}D_d$, and $D(p)=\operatorname{Spec}P_p$. Restricting $f$ and $g$ gives maps into $V$ (restriction to an open target is a restriction of the same locally ringed space map). By the affine spectrum correspondence these give ring maps $B\to A_a$ and $B\to T_t$. Their maps to $D_d$ agree because $f$ and $g$ agree on $E$. Sending $b$ to the pair of its images, followed by the inverse of step 2, gives a ring map $B\to P_p$. Its spectrum is a morphism $h_{p,V}:D(p)\to V\to Z$ with the prescribed restrictions on $D(a)$ and $D(t)$. Joint surjectivity of $Y,W\to Q$ then shows its underlying map is $h|_{D(p)}$.

source.place: Tag 0ET0, lemma-basic-example-pushout, structure sheaf identification and induced ringed-space map, realized on the principal affine basis

proof.text: We record the local uniqueness needed for gluing. For any $r=(a_r,t_r)\in P$ and any affine target $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$, two morphisms $D(r)\to V$ agreeing after precomposition from $D(a_r)$ and $D(t_r)$ are equal: their ring maps $B\to P_r$ have equal composites to $A_{a_r}$ and $T_{t_r}$, so they are equal by the injection in step 2, and the affine spectrum correspondence gives equality of the morphisms. This is only injectivity on a principal affine chart with affine target; it does not assert the pushout property for arbitrary target schemes.

source.place: Tag 0ET0, lemma-basic-example-pushout, uniqueness of the induced sheaf map; elementary affine-coordinate calculation using step 2

proof.text: The morphisms $h_{p,V}$ agree on overlaps. At a point $q$ of $D(p)\cap D(p')$, choose an affine open $V''$ containing $h(q)$ inside $V\cap V'$; this is possible by local affineness, without claiming $V\cap V'$ affine. Choose a principal neighbourhood $D(r)$ of $q$ contained in $D(p)\cap D(p')\cap h^{-1}(V'')$. Both constructed maps restrict to morphisms $D(r)\to V''$, because their underlying maps are $h$. Their composites with $D(a_r)$ and $D(t_r)$ are the restrictions of $f$ and $g$, respectively, so step 5 makes them equal on $D(r)$. Such opens cover the overlap. The uniqueness clause of scheme-morphism gluing makes the maps equal on the whole overlap; its existence clause now glues the $h_{p,V}$ to a morphism $\widetilde h:Q\to Z$. Its composites with $Y$ and $W$ equal $f$ and $g$ by the same uniqueness clause on the inverse-image open covers.

source.place: Tag 01JA, section-glueing-schemes, mapping property in lemma-glue; Tag 04TN, sheaves-lemma-glue-maps; Tag 01IT, lemma-basis-affine-opens; principal-affine realization of Tag 0ET0

proof.text: If $k:Q\to Z$ is any other compatible scheme morphism, the topological uniqueness in [lem-sfb-fibre-product-spectrum-topology] gives $|k|=h$. Hence, on every pair $(p,V)$ of step 3, $k|_{D(p)}$ factors through $V$. It agrees with $h_{p,V}$ on the two inverse-image principal opens, since both extend $f$ and $g$. Step 5 yields equality on $D(p)$; scheme-morphism gluing yields $k=\widetilde h$. Thus every compatible pair has exactly one extension, which is precisely the colimit universal property for the finite span defining the pushout. If $Q$ is empty the open cover is empty and the same gluing statement supplies existence and uniqueness. All the preceding arguments allow zero rings and require neither finiteness nor Noetherianity.

source.place: Tag 0ET0, lemma-basic-example-pushout, universal property and uniqueness; local affine realization
